results.title: The researcher of 2026: Human judgment in an AI-first world
results.content: # The researcher of 2026: Human judgment in an AI-first world. When an entire sector hits that level of adoption, the question is no longer whether AI will reshape research workflows – it’s how researchers will respond. Researchers aren’t treating AI as a novel add-on. These aren’t hypothetical scenarios – they’re daily frictions that shape what teams will and won’t hand over to AI. ## **What emerges is a new model: The human-led, AI-supported research team**. Researchers do not envision a future in which AI replaces them. ## **AI won’t reduce the amount of research – it will increase it**. One of the most surprising findings in the study is that teams expect to do more research in an AI-driven world, not less. The future researcher is not someone who simply uses AI. By 2026, the researchers who thrive will be the ones who treat AI as a co-analyst – not a crutch, not a gimmick, and not a threat. AI will not define the future of research.
